headline: Arabian Travel Market opens with focus on Gulf tourism recovery and regional travel trends
deck: The 33rd Arabian Travel Market at Dubai World Trade Centre features 2,400+ exhibitors and 50,000+ international visitors exploring tourism recovery, hotel development and travel technology for Arabian Gulf destinations.
excerpt: Arabian Travel Market opens on 16 September, bringing together tour operators, hotel groups, destination marketing organisations and travel technology companies to negotiate partnerships and explore emerging trends in Gulf tourism, hospitality and travel infrastructure.
content:
Arabian Travel Market opens on 16 September at Dubai World Trade Centre, running through 18 September with 2,400+ exhibitors and 50,000+ international visitors including tour operators, hotel groups, airlines, destination marketing organisations, travel technology companies and media. The market encompasses 10 halls focusing on destination promotion, hotel and hospitality services, travel technology, adventure and niche tourism segments.

Tourism recovery across the Gulf continues post-pandemic. Saudi Arabia's tourism authority reported 65 million international and domestic visitors in 2025, with targets of 100 million annual visitors by 2030 through expansion of visa accessibility and hospitality infrastructure. The UAE received 18.7 million international visitors in 2025, with focus on diversification beyond Dubai city tourism into regional experiences and nature-based tourism. Qatar has positioned itself as a gateway destination post-FIFA World Cup 2022, with expanded airline capacity and hotel infrastructure supporting leisure and MICE (meetings, incentives, conferences, exhibitions) tourism.

Hotel development pipeline reflects tourism growth expectations. New luxury hotel openings in Saudi Arabia include projects in Riyadh, Jeddah and Neom, with focus on experiential hospitality and design-led properties. The UAE's hotel inventory expansion addresses growing mid-market and lifestyle segments, with boutique hotel concepts and serviced apartment models capturing changing travel preferences. Beach resort and luxury destination management companies are expanding across Red Sea regions and Gulf coastal zones.

Travel technology platforms showcase innovations in booking experiences, dynamic pricing, and personalisation. Artificial intelligence algorithms analyse traveller preferences and booking patterns to optimise room inventory and pricing across property portfolios. Mobile-first platforms provide seamless pre-arrival, in-stay and post-departure guest experiences. Blockchain-based loyalty programmes enable redemption flexibility across hotel chains and partner travel services.

Niche tourism segments including adventure travel, cultural heritage tourism, wellness retreats and ecotourism are growing market shares. Adventure operators expand offerings in desert expeditions, mountain trekking, water sports and extreme sports experiences across Gulf destinations. Heritage tourism focuses on restored traditional villages, Islamic art museums and historical site development. Wellness tourism combines luxury spa facilities, health-focused dining and regenerative tourism experiences aligned with regional wellness movements.

MICE tourism represents 25-30 percent of international visitors to Gulf destinations. Convention centres including Dubai World Trade Centre, Riyadh International Convention Centre and Doha Exhibition and Convention Centre are expanding capacity and technology capabilities to support large-scale events, exhibitions and conferences.

The Arabian Travel Market runs until 18 September.

Digital transformation in travel is reshaping customer experiences and business models. Mobile-first booking platforms, real-time pricing, personalised recommendations and seamless payment systems are becoming baseline expectations. AI chatbots handle customer service inquiries 24/7, reducing operational costs and improving response times. Augmented reality hotel tours and virtual destination experiences allow customers to preview properties and locations before booking.

Regional airline capacity expansion is critical infrastructure supporting tourism growth. New aircraft deliveries and route expansions by Emirates, Etihad, Saudi Arabian Airlines and new entrants like flydubai and Air Arabia are increasing seat capacity and flight frequency. Open skies agreements and liberal bilateral air service agreements within GCC facilitate regional connectivity and support tourism growth.

Post-pandemic tourism patterns show sustained shift toward short-haul regional travel and domestic tourism. Staycation trends in Gulf states reflect geographic convenience and perceived pandemic safety. Adventure tourism and wellness retreats capture travellers seeking outdoor experiences and health-focused hospitality. Multi-destination packages combining desert safaris, beach resorts and city tourism are attracting higher-value traveller segments willing to spend more for curated experiences.
